seaweed-kelp-foods.name: Seaweed / kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — dried, as sold)

MeHg.label: Seaweed is a marine primary producer, not a predator; methylmercury does not biomagnify into algae, so it is a negligible fraction of total mercury. No seaweed methylmercury ML exists; the general-fishery methylmercury value (Mexico NOM-242 other fishery products, 500) is read across only to establish the bound, and it is subsumed by the far stricter dried-seaweed total-mercury ceiling. Methylmercury is governed by and bounded by tHg.

Cr.label: Read-across from the GB 2762-2025 total-chromium maximum level for cereals (1000 ug/kg), GB's own dry plant-food line; no sovereign sets total chromium for dried seaweed, milk powder (2000) is not a plant analog, and GB's aquatic-animal line (2000) concurs as the ceiling (M2 adjudication 2026-09-02 (two blind Fable verifiers agreed)).

Al.label: No government sets an aluminium contaminant ML for food; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI. Read-across to the nearest food aluminium instrument (China GB 2760 baked-foods aluminium, 100000) as a monitor/baseline ceiling. Seaweed accumulates aluminium naturally; this ceiling flags gross contamination while clean product passes. Flagged monitor/baseline, not per-lot-critical.

Sn.label: Tin is a can-migration analyte; dried seaweed foods are sold in non-metal packaging with no tinplate contact, and no government sets a tin ML for seaweed. Read-across to the EU 2023/915 general canned-food inorganic-tin ML (200000) as a packaging-migration baseline; with no tin source clean product passes, and a mispackaged or contaminated sample fails.

Pb.label: government read-across: China GB 2762-2025 Table 1 item 6.3 lead 1.0 mg/kg for algae products (excluding spirulina products), product as placed on the market; the strictest in-force sovereign lead ceiling for a dried seaweed product. Replaces the Israel MoH 2016 dried-seaweed row (5000), which the Ministry marks not in force since 19.02.2026 (M1 verification 2026-09-02); a tightening from 5000 to 1000.

tAs.label: disclosed species-as-total ceiling (audit exception C6d): no in-force government sets a total-arsenic ML for seaweed (the Israel MoH 2016 dried-seaweed row, 5000, is not in force since 19.02.2026), so total arsenic is held at the AU-NZ Schedule 19 inorganic-arsenic seaweed limit of 1 mg/kg; because inorganic arsenic is a component of total arsenic, a total at or below 1000 guarantees the inorganic species is too. This is a protective read-across in the species-to-total direction only, never the reverse.

shellfish.name: Shellfish (crustaceans and bivalve molluscs, not canned)

MeHg.label: No mollusc/crustacean-specific methylmercury ML below the general-fishery value applies. Read-across to the general/other-fishery methylmercury ML (Mexico NOM-242 other fishery products, 500), stricter than the crustacean-specific 1000 and more protective for low-trophic shellfish. Held at or below the total-mercury ceiling.

Ni.label: Read-across from Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 nickel in baby food except juices (500 ug/kg, product as placed on market): no sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for fish, crustaceans, molluscs or cephalopods, and the wet-basis baby-food row, whose scope includes fish-based foods, is the nearest same-basis instrument; the dry husked-rice row (2000) the standard previously cited is a different basis and was refuted by M2 adjudication 2026-09-02 (two blind Fable verifiers agreed).

Sn.label: Tin is a can-migration analyte; no government sets a tin ML for non-canned seafood (every seafood tin ML is canned/tinplate-only). Read-across to the EU 2023/915 general canned-food inorganic-tin ML (200000) as a packaging-migration baseline; fresh/frozen shellfish has no tin source and passes. Canned shellfish is certified under the canned-seafood subcategory.

Al.label: No government sets an aluminium contaminant ML for food; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI. Read-across to the nearest food aluminium instrument (China GB 2760 baked-foods aluminium, 100000) as a monitor/baseline ceiling; shellfish aluminium sits below it, so clean product passes while gross contamination fails. Flagged monitor/baseline, not per-lot-critical.

cephalopods.name: Cephalopods (octopus, squid, cuttlefish; not canned)

MeHg.label: No government sets a cephalopod-specific methylmercury ML. Read across from the non-predatory / general fishery MeHg value (Mexico NOM-242, other fishery products, 500 ug/kg): cephalopods are not high-trophic mercury accumulators, so the non-predatory fish MeHg tier is the nearest defensible value. Held at or below the total-mercury ceiling.

canned-seafood.name: Canned seafood (canned tuna, canned fish)

iAs.label: EU 2025/1891 inorganic arsenic 100 ug/kg for muscle meat of fish (species other than the listed higher-iAs group). No government sets an iAs ML specific to canned tuna; tuna is not in the EU listed-500 group, so it takes the general fish-muscle iAs floor.

Ni.label: Read-across from Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 nickel in baby food except juices (500 ug/kg, product as placed on market): no sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for fish, crustaceans, molluscs or cephalopods, and the wet-basis baby-food row, whose scope includes fish-based foods, is the nearest same-basis instrument; the dry husked-rice row (2000) the standard previously cited is a different basis and was refuted by M2 adjudication 2026-09-02 (two blind Fable verifiers agreed).

Cd.label: Costa Rica RTCR 409:2008 cadmium in fish in general (50 ug/kg), concurred by Guyana and Fiji general-fish rows; the GSO 193:2021 general row (also 50) is not cited because its own exception rows govern tuna (100), sardine and anchovy (250) and mackerel (100), species this row names (M2 adjudication 2026-09-02 (two blind Fable verifiers agreed)).

MeHg.label: GB 2762-2025 methylmercury in aquatic animals and their products other than predatory fish (500 ug/kg); canned tuna is a predatory-fish product governed at 1000 (FDA CPG 540.600; MX NOM-242) and is certified to the stricter 500 as the group minimum, disclosed here (M2 adjudication 2026-09-02 (two blind Fable verifiers agreed)).

_doc: Category-6 (Seafood) config. Species-specific dual-mercury (tHg+MeHg), arsenic iAs+tAs, canned-tin gating, dedicated cephalopod subcategory. Built by derive workflow ws6q2oktn and corrected by adversarial audit wf_925293b1-55f (predatory Cd 100->50 CR general-fish; canned tHg/MeHg/Cd 1000/1000/100->500/500/50 general-fish floor; freshwater tHg 500->300 EU lower-mercury/trout; seaweed basis as_sold dried; cephalopods added) against the complete 2634-row register. 2026-08-25 Certification-Readiness completion: panel expanded to the full 11-analyte certification panel; every no-ML cell now carries a disclosed numeric limit-of-record. MeHg resolves to the strictest species-appropriate government methylmercury ML (predatory 1000, general/other-fishery 500) and is published firm where it is at or below the binding total-mercury ceiling (predatory/canned/shellfish), else bounded by tHg (reconcile threshold strict >). Ni read-across EU 2024/1987 husked-rice 2000 (matrix-nearest, occurrence-cleared; no animal-seafood nickel ML exists); Cr-VI read-across CA SWRCB drinking-water 10 (kept <= total Cr); non-canned Sn read-across EU 2023/915 canned-food inorganic tin 200000 (packaging-migration baseline); Al read-across China GB 2760 baked-foods 100000 (monitor/baseline; occurrence up to ~34000 in canned product would fail the generic 1000 FCM anchor); seaweed total Cr read-across China GB 2762 milk-powder 2000 (monitor; Cr-VI is the binding health control).
_scope_note_2026_09_02: 2026-09-02: GB 2762-2025 rows entered the register. Two scope false positives were caught by the round-trip diff and fixed here, never in the register: (1) the condiments total-arsenic row (Table 4 item 8.1, whose scope text reads 'excluding aquatic condiments') matched the fish scopes' 'aquatic' include and would have bound canned seafood and non-predatory fish at 500 in place of the live 1000; 'condiment' is now excluded. (2) the aquatic-animals methylmercury row (Table 3 item 1.1, 'excluding predatory fish') matched the predatory subcategory's 'predator' include; 'excluding predator' is now excluded so the predatory row (item 1.2, 1000) binds instead. Part 2 direction: toward the literature (each instrument applied within its own stated scope).
